question: What is the meaning of mixtures list in relation to physical composition?
description: The meaning of mixtures list in relation to physical composition refers to the comprehensive list of components and materials, including their features such as size, volume, density, amount, allocation, material, at various levels in the component tree, and the relationship between the components.

3.1.3
Composition properties
Figure 5 shows the composition property facet. This block of ontology helps to optimise
the selection, processing, and assembly of the constituent parts and materials of a product
and facilitates their separation, dismantling, and recycling at the end of life of a product
to maximise the circularity.
Figure 5: Composition property facet of the MPO.
CompositionProperty has two subclasses, ConstituentPart and ConstituentMaterial. For
example, crossbeam has constituent materials carbon fibre, glass fibre, epoxy resin, alu-
minium, foam, and film adhesive that have mass, and a source and destination in a circular
economy.

a E.g., reflected by scarcity score: short-medium-long term, the dependency score (can other materials be used if we run out), supply-security score (is the material 
available in our region, and future scarcity related legislative requirements. 
b Listing the materials and quantities that are expected as waste (e.g., expressed in European Waste Catalogue (EWC) categories). 
c Physical composition refers to the full list of components and materials (or bill of materials, including its features such as size, volume, densitiy, amount, allocation, 
material, at various level in the component tree, and the relationship between the components (i.e., how the components are used in the products.) 
d The technical characteristics include, but are not limited to, geometry, spatial relationships, quantities, location and properties of building elements, class 
strengths, densities, fillings, adjuvants, binders, blend compositions, granulate size. 
e E.g., resistance scores against emissions, emission tests, chemical compositions, toxic materials, exposed time to substances, etc. 
f This is the opposite of listing hazardous substances. It lists the safe materials that were used. 
g This measures the performance as specified during the design and validates this with the current object performance. 
h Reflects the total negative environmental effects based on the amount of disposed elements and using LCA data.
